# Model validation report: Aegis conformal risk engine

<!-- Generated by `python main.py model-card` from site/public/data. Do not edit by hand. -->

Structured after the Federal Reserve's SR 11-7 guidance on model risk management: purpose, data,
assumptions, performance against an incumbent, sensitivity, limitations and ongoing monitoring.
This is a self-assessment by the model's developer, not an independent validation, and the model
is a research project, not one used to manage money.

**Data as of 2026-10-30** · test period 2020-01-02 to 2026-10-23
(1,712 trading days) · run `e63fc0b` · Aegis 0.1.0

## 1. Summary

| | |
|---|---|
| Model | Five-day portfolio volatility forecast with a conformal 95% interval, plus one-day VaR and Expected Shortfall |
| Champion | Adaptive conformal inference (ACI), γ = 0.005, absolute-residual score |
| Incumbent | Gaussian EWMA (RiskMetrics), λ = 0.94 |
| Verdict | **Fit for purpose as a calibrated risk forecast.** ACI holds its 95% promise overall (95.0%) and through 2020 (94.5%); its 99% VaR passes Kupiec (p 0.783) and stays in the Basel green zone on 98.8% of days, against 56.4% for the incumbent. |
| Findings against | 99% breaches cluster (Christoffersen p 0.008); calibration costs more capital than the incumbent (30.6% vs 18.0%); filtered historical simulation is as well calibrated for less (19.3%). |

## 2. Purpose and intended use

The model answers one question each trading day: *how volatile will this portfolio be over the
next 5 days, and how sure can I be?* It returns a point forecast of realized
volatility, an interval that should contain the outcome 95% of the time, and one-day VaR
and Expected Shortfall. Intended uses are risk limits, volatility targeting and capital estimates
for a small multi-asset portfolio. It is not intended for single-name risk, intraday risk,
options, or as a return forecast.

## 3. Data

| | |
|---|---|
| Source | yfinance daily adjusted closes; VIX as a feature; 139 FOMC statements (not used, section 7) |
| Portfolio | Equal weights in SPY, TLT, GLD, USO, rebalanced daily |
| History | 2010-01-05 to 2026-10-30 |
| Training | 2010-02-04 to 2017-12-21 (1,986 days): point model fit |
| Calibration | 2018-01-02 to 2019-12-23 (498 days): conformal scores |
| Test | 2020-01-02 to 2026-10-23 (1,712 days): never seen in fitting |
| Embargo | 5 days between splits, so overlapping 5-day targets can't leak |

Prices are free Yahoo Finance data, so dividend and split adjustments are Yahoo's. Look-ahead is
guarded by tests that perturb data after a date and check that nothing known on that date changes.

## 4. Methodology and assumptions

1. **Point model.** Ridge regression on HAR-style realized-volatility lags, EWMA volatilities
   and the VIX level and change, predicting log 5-day realized volatility (out-of-fold RMSE 0.420).
2. **Conformal layer.** Absolute residuals on the calibration set give the initial cut-off. ACI then
   moves its working miss rate by γ after every observed hit or miss, with outcomes arriving
   5 days late, and a floor of 0.2·α so it can't run to an infinite interval.
3. **VaR and ES.** One-sided conformal lower bounds on next-day portfolio return. ES uses the average
   calibration score beyond the VaR cut-off.

Key assumption: split conformal assumes calibration and test errors are exchangeable. Markets
violate this (section 5); ACI drops the assumption and instead guarantees long-run average coverage
for any sequence, at the cost of reacting only after misses.

Test period 2020–2026. VaR breach targets are 5% and 1%; Kupiec tests the breach rate,
Christoffersen tests whether breaches cluster (p below 0.05 rejects). ES Z2 is the Acerbi–Székely
statistic (near zero is good, strongly negative means risk understated). Basel columns use a
trailing 250-day window from 1,462 scored days.

| ACI                     |  94.5% |  94.4% |  96.4% |  95.6% |  97.2% |  92.4% |  94.6% |      93.7% |     96.8% |          94.6% |
| Gaussian EWMA           |  89.7% |  93.3% |  94.8% |  95.6% |  98.4% |  93.6% |  92.6% |      94.0% |     96.0% |          92.1% |

| Mondrian (VIX terciles) |  94.9% |  93.3% |  98.0% |  97.6% |  97.6% |  93.6% |  97.5% |      91.6% |     98.8% |          97.7% |

The textbook split method under-covers in the 2020 crash (88.9%); ACI holds 94.5%.
ACI's weakest year is 2025 (92.4%). Mondrian conformal (separate cut-offs per VIX tercile) lifts stressed-market
coverage but under-covers calm markets because the tercile boundaries drifted after calibration.

| EWMA λ         |   Point RMSE |   ACI coverage |   ACI width |   Gaussian 99% VaR breaches |
|----------------|--------------|----------------|-------------|-----------------------------|
| 0.9            |        0.425 |          95.0% |       1.732 |                       1.93% |
| 0.94 (default) |        0.428 |          95.0% |       1.738 |                       1.93% |

Across every α, γ and λ tested, ACI coverage is within 0.25 points of its target. The settings
change width, not calibration.

## 7. Limitations and known weaknesses

1. **Clustered tail breaches.** At 99%, ACI's breach rate is on target (0.93%) but breaches
   bunch (Christoffersen p 0.008). It adapts after a miss, so the first days of a shock get through.
2. **Capital cost.** Being calibrated costs capital: mean Basel charge 30.6% of portfolio value for ACI
   against 18.0% for the incumbent.
3. **A classical model does as well.** Filtered historical simulation passes both tests at 99%
   (Kupiec p 0.832, Christoffersen p 0.182) with 19.3% capital. Conformal's
   advantage is that it needs no model of the return distribution, not superior calibration.
4. **Text adds nothing on real data.** FOMC statements raised forecast error by 1.2%
   with the lexicon, so the production configuration is price-only.
5. **Narrow evidence.** One four-asset portfolio, one test period with one crash, free data, flat
   5 bp trading costs. The 10-day regulatory test has only 171 non-overlapping windows.

**Issues found in development and fixed** (each now has a regression test):

- The SLM schema invited sign errors; direction-named fields took sign agreement from 72% to 100%.
- At 99%, ACI's working level could reach zero after a cluster of misses, giving infinite VaR for
  years; the floor in section 4 fixes it.
- Metrics silently dropped infinite-VaR days, flattering the breach rate; they now count as days
  and are reported separately.
- DtACI under-covered with delayed feedback until its experts were scored on the levels actually issued.

## 8. Ongoing monitoring

The data refreshes every weeknight. A breach of any trigger below calls for a recalibration review:
re-check the calibration window, refit the point model, and re-run this report.

| Statistic                                      | Trigger                 |   Value on 2026-10-23 | Status   |
|------------------------------------------------|-------------------------|-----------------------|----------|
| Coverage of the 95% interval, trailing 63 days | below 85%               |                 98.4% | ok       |
| 99% VaR exceptions, trailing 250 days (Basel)  | 5 or more (yellow zone) |                     3 | ok       |
| Kupiec p, 99% VaR, trailing 250 days           | below 0.05              |                 0.758 | ok       |
| Nightly data refresh (`status.json`)           | failed                  |             succeeded | ok       |

Over the test period the coverage trigger would have fired on 4.2% of days (in
2020 and 2025) and the Basel trigger on 1.2% (in 2025): rare enough
not to cry wolf, but not silent in a stress period.

Further triggers that need a person: a change in portfolio composition, a structural market change
(new volatility regime outside the calibration range), or a change to any model setting in section 6.

## 9. Reproduction

```bash
pip install -e .
python main.py fetch -c configs/default.yaml
python main.py backtest -c configs/default.yaml
python main.py sensitivity -c configs/default.yaml
python main.py export-site -c configs/default.yaml
python main.py model-card -c configs/default.yaml
```
